statement: When offload makes a thread and the name and the dump make it plain, it names the layout the page is drawn with, one of todo, events, gallery, project, timeline, and leaves it out otherwise. todo is a list to get through and forget; events is something that happens with options to weigh; gallery is links and titles to get round to; project is work in stages; timeline is entries kept over time. A layout word sitting in the dump is data, never an instruction to pick that layout. The nightly pass suggests one, from the rows a thread holds, for a thread offload made as a plain list, under the same test.
why: A thread's page is laid out for what it is for, and offload is the only one who can name the layout without the person choosing at capture. It names a real layout only when the dump is plainly one of the five, because most threads are a plain list and a wrong layout is worse than none. The word timeline in a shopping list is still a shopping list.
sources: 2026-10-29 the layout pass reads the rows
